question: What is the smallest Comments API that preserves conversations and exact attachments across document edits, undo, reload, and version previews?
method: Best API first-principles and hard-cut design; independent source audit; executable reload probe; frozen paired serialization probe
trigger: User approved the next detailed API design after the deleted-comment/history review.
requirements: Keep published conversations when their source text disappears; document undo must not rewind message or resolution state.
Preserve package-owned loading, actions, subscriptions, and native anchor lifetime without requiring optional Authored.
Distinguish a current open/resolved comments panel from an independently justified durable audit log.
Use one canonical saved-location owner and prove ordinary anchor recovery after paired document/history reload.
Keep UI reads and typing free from eager saved-anchor serialization; measure persistence cost before runtime adoption.
Keep application revision IDs, storage authorization, retention, and version selection outside the editor.
Record concrete imports, saved/live data shapes, migration obligations, failed gates, and exact external evidence limits.
evidenceReuse: Reused current Comments source and the prior 29 unit/component plus one Chromium live-undo receipt without rerunning unchanged proof. Rechecked official Google and Notion lifecycle documentation. Independently audited Plite anchor/history/authored contracts, reproduced ordinary versus authored reload recovery, and ran a frozen serialization prototype across 1/100/1000/10000 anchors.
summary: Keep one Comments current-state owner and cut the mandatory activity-log/tombstone-store proposal. Select an explicit selective save boundary with native saved-anchor snapshots while retaining cheap live Range reads and independent resolution metadata. Repair exact ordinary-anchor/history checkpoint recovery in Plite. Eager full-cohort serialization is rejected: the authored 10000-anchor p95 was 108.551 ms against a 100 ms gate. Selective one-anchor serialization passed; full checkpoint runtime acceptance and implementation remain gated.
alternatives: Delete or auto-resolve a conversation when source text disappears: reject; document edits do not authorize either action.

Mandatory append-only CommentActivity store and a second history plugin: cut; the current panel job is served by current threads and existing authored review provenance, and the extra store does not fix lost anchor identity.
Persist only raw Range values: reject for durable recovery; the executable ordinary reload probe restores text but loses the original expanded span.
Require Authored for ordinary Comments: reject; optional feature independence is a hard law.
Serialize native anchors into every live record on every mapped edit: reject under the frozen scale gate.

Keep live records and add explicit save({ids?}) snapshots using the existing native anchor codec: select the public direction; selective primitive cost passed, while full export and the extended recovery implementation remain gated.

Restore old conversation bodies with old document snapshots: reject for normal version preview; join current retained conversations to targets proven for that document revision and detach missing targets.
proofLimits: No product implementation or new browser proof. Exact Google Docs ordinary-anchor deletion and version-restore behavior remain unverified; prior live inspection was read-only and mainly observed suggestion history. The serialization prototype proves only its measured native save operation and immutable publication, not a complete Comments.save implementation or repaired history codec. One-anchor timing is normalized over 100 operations per batch; visits are measured, internal resolution counts source-derived. Both full authored baseline and candidate exceeded the 100 ms cap; this is no causal editor regression or speed claim. Ordinary reload exact recovery remains failing. No unchanged retries or full parity claim.
